title: Bram and the Hymn
premise: Hazel Kavanagh, a meticulous pest controller who trusts only what he can document, is hired to investigate sounds in the walls of St. Brannoc's church in the dying village of Hollowmere. He discovers claw-marks with human fingerprints and learns the village's original bell—melted down in 1911 after a child's death—was recast into a new bell that was never hung, its bronze buried beneath the church floor. The founding families' descendants have been feeding something for a century: an inheritance of guilt that demands a bell-ringer every harvest. When the vanished bell begins ringing on its own, Hazel realizes he was summoned not to exterminate but to be offered, and he must survive until sunrise by documenting the truth aloud—the one thing the thing in the tower cannot abide—to break the covenant before the harvest moon rises.
about_author: Wren Almeida is the pen name of a former parish archivist from the West Country who spent years cataloguing church records of bells, burials, and unexplained silences. Their fiction blends procedural precision with folk horror, exploring how communities bury their sins in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Hazel Kavanagh, POV. A routine call about scratching in St. Brannoc's vestry wall; Hazel photographs everything, as always, because documentation is his prayer against chaos. He finds droppings that are too large and a smear on the plaster shaped like a handprint with too many knuckles. Emotional beat: professional calm masking a flicker of unease.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Lab results come back impossible: the prints in the grease-smear are human, adult, and dated by oxidation to roughly 1911. The vicar, Reverend Ilsa Marsh, deflects his questions and asks him to sign an oddly specific liability waiver. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. He canvasses the village; doors close politely but firmly. An old woman, Edith Pryce, slips him a note: 'Ask about the bell.' At the pub, the landlord's laughter dies when Hazel mentions 1911. Emotional beat: the slow realization that the whole village is holding its breath.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV, intercut with Edith's spoken testimony. Parish records show the original bell was melted down after a child drowned in the mill race—the villagers blamed the bell's tolling. Its bronze was supposedly sold, but no receipt exists. Emotional beat: grief surfacing under bureaucratic dust.

chapters.title: Scratching at Three
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. He stakes out the church overnight with cameras. At 3:11 a.m., the scratching moves upward—from the crypt toward the empty belfry—and stops directly above him. His camera records forty seconds of static and a sound like wet knuckles flexing. Emotional beat: dread replacing procedure.

chapters.title: Waiver and Warning
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. The six descendant families—the 'Founders'—summon him to a meeting. They offer triple his fee to leave, then veiled threats when he refuses. He notices each of them wears a small bronze ring, cast from the same metal. Emotional beat: anger at being bought, resolve to stay.

chapters.title: Edith's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edith Pryce, POV. She shows Hazel her grandmother's ledger: every harvest since 1911, a name entered and struck through—a ringer 'invited up' to the tower. The last entry is blank except for tomorrow's date and two words: 'the outsider.' Emotional beat: complicity and terror entwined.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Research montage: the child, Tomas Pryce, didn't drown—he was given to the bell to stop a blight, and the blight stopped. The melting was never a burial; it was a feeding. Something in the bronze kept the ledger going even without a bell to ring. Emotional beat: horror of inherited sin.

chapters.title: The Crypt Door
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. He breaks into the crypt and finds the recast bell, never hung, sunk into the floor like a wound. Around it, the stone is worn smooth in a circle, as if walked for a century. Fingerprints in the dust—hundreds, all the same small hands. Tomas's hands. Emotional beat: pity piercing fear.

chapters.title: They Know
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. His van is burned in the night; his hotel room searched, notebooks missing—but not his hidden duplicates. Reverend Marsh warns him gently to go, revealing she is a Founder's daughter who chose the church over the covenant. Emotional beat: isolation, and the first true ally.

chapters.title: First Toll
chapters.summary: Village chorus POV (rotating brief sections). At dusk, though there is no bell in the tower, the bell rings—one clean note heard across Hollowmere. Dogs howl. The Founders assemble in the churchyard without being called. Emotional beat: collective guilt finally audible.

chapters.title: The Rite of Invitation
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. He witnesses the Founders perform the centenary rite: they formally 'invite' him to the tower, reading his name into the ledger. Refusal, Edith explains, doesn't void it—it only means the thing comes down to fetch him. Emotional beat: claustrophobic inevitability.

chapters.title: Sunrise Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. He calculates: the harvest moon rises at 8:42 p.m.; sunrise is 6:58 a.m. If he survives the night, the invitation lapses—but no invited ringer has ever seen dawn. He prepares: salt, recordings, printed documents, and a plan to read the truth aloud from the tower. Emotional beat: grim methodical courage.

chapters.title: Marsh's Confession
chapters.summary: Reverend Marsh, POV. She tells Hazel her own father was the last ringer, taken in 1961, and that she has spent her life unable to say it aloud. She gives him the one relic that matters: the original 1911 bell charter naming Tomas Pryce as 'given, not lost.' Emotional beat: shame transmuted into aid.

chapters.title: Moonrise
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. The harvest moon clears the ridge. Every door in Hollowmere opens; the Founders walk to the church not by choice but by covenant. The tower door, locked for a century, stands open. Hazel walks in, recording everything. Emotional beat: terrible calm before the ascent.

chapters.title: The Climb
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. The stair spirals past a century of residue: names scratched into the stone, small handprints, older rings of wear beneath newer ones. Something climbs with him, matching his pace, breathing through the walls. Emotional beat: escalating terror held in check by ritual—counting steps, narrating aloud.

chapters.title: The Belfry
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. At the top: no bell, but the air itself tolls. The presence manifests as a child-shaped absence wearing fingerprints, reaching for him—not malicious, but hungry to be remembered. It wants a ringer because it wants someone to stay. Emotional beat: heartbreak inside horror.

chapters.title: Read It Aloud
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Cornered, he does the only thing left: he reads the charter, the ledger, the lab report, the truth of Tomas's murder—aloud, into his recorder, into the dark. Each documented fact lands like a hammer-blow; the tolling falters. Emotional beat: documentation as exorcism, prayer made literal.

chapters.title: The Founders Below
chapters.summary: Founders' chorus POV. In the churchyard, the families hear the truth spoken from their own tower and feel the covenant snap link by link. Some kneel; some flee; old Aldous Vane screams that they can still renew it. Emotional beat: a community's sins dragged into light.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. The presence, named and witnessed, stops reaching and simply listens—then, as the sun crests, it lets go, taking its fingerprints off the world. The tower falls silent. Hazel descends at 6:58 a.m., alive, the first ringer to see dawn. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Recasting
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV, weeks later. The Founders face exposure; Marsh proposes digging up the bell and truly melting it—with Tomas's name read into the record first. Edith burns the ledger page by page. Hazel files his final report, addressed to no authority, archived anyway. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Hymn
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV, epilogue. Driving away, he passes a schoolyard where children sing a hymn he's never heard—words matching phrases from the charter. He stops, listens, and understands some inheritances must be sung out rather than buried. He drives on as the last note fades. Emotional beat: haunted peace.
